body.text: How do you combine Myra's Lycian rock tombs, Roman theatre and St. Nicholas Church?

Start at Myra Ruins when gates open at 08:30 AM to photograph the cliffside Lycian rock tombs and Roman theatre in soft morning light before tour buses arrive from Antalya. Then drive five minutes into central Demre for the shaded interior of St. Nicholas Church, finishing both sites comfortably in three hours.

Myra was one of the six leading cities of the Lycian League and later served as the Roman provincial capital of Lycia ([Turkish Museums: Myra Ruins](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/1966-antalya-myra-orenyeri/1966/1)). Its two-part archaeological zone requires very little uphill climbing: the semi-circular Roman theatre sits directly beneath honeycomb clusters of fourth-century BCE temple-façade tombs carved to mimic Lycian timber houses, with theatrical stone masks displayed along the lower walkway.

Five minutes south in Demre town sits the [Antalya St. Nicholas Memorial Museum](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/1956-antalya-st-nicholas-memorial-museum/1956/4), a Byzantine basilica built over the fourth-century church where Bishop Nicholas of Myra served. Inside the sunken nave, visitors walk past opus sectile marble floors, restored 11th-century frescoes, and the broken marble sarcophagus linked to the saint before Italian merchants removed his relics to Bari in 1087.
How far is Demre from Kaş and Kekova?

Demre sits about 47 km east of Kaş—a scenic 50-to-60-minute drive along the winding D400 coastal highway—and roughly 20 km east of Üçağız village, the main harbor for Kekova sunken-city boat trips. Travelers staying in Kaş can easily combine Demre's archaeological sites with an afternoon Kekova boat outing in one relaxed day.

If you are driving from Antalya or Olympos rather than Kaş, expect roughly 2 hours 15 minutes from Antalya city center or 1 hour 15 minutes from Adrasan via Finike's coastal cliffs. Parking is straightforward at both Myra Ruins (signed lot right beside the entrance) and central Demre near St. Nicholas Square, though midday tour-bus arrivals briefly crowd the church courtyard between 11:00 AM and 1:30 PM.
What are the 2026 ticket fees and MuseumPass rules?

In 2026, official foreign-visitor tickets cost €13 for Myra Ruins and €17 for the St. Nicholas Memorial Museum—€30 combined. Both sites are operated by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and accept the 15-day MuseumPass Türkiye (€165) and the 7-day MuseumPass The Mediterranean (€90), each allowing one entry per site.

Tickets are priced in euros and charged at the daily exchange rate in Turkish lira at site ticket booths or purchased online as e-tickets through the official Ministry portal ([Myra E-Ticket](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-MYR01-87-009); [St. Nicholas E-Ticket](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-STN01-87-009)).

body.text: Verify regional coverage on the official [MuseumPass Akdeniz page](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-25-009) or [MuseumPass Türkiye page](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-27-009) before buying. Children under eight enter Ministry sites free with passport verification.
Where do you stop for lunch near Üçağız?

Skip the bus-group buffets beside Myra's parking lot and drive 25 minutes west to Üçağız harbor, where family-run waterfront restaurants serve grilled sea bream, calamari, and olive-oil mezes directly over the calm Kekova lagoon. Alternatively, stop at Çayağzı (Andriake) harbor ten minutes from Demre if you are pairing lunch with the Lycian Civilizations Museum.

Üçağız is a compact fishing village with wooden jetties jutting into protected waters facing Kaleköy (Simena). Arriving around 12:30 PM lets you eat at a shaded dockside table while booking or meeting a private wooden boat for a two-to-three-hour afternoon loop past the sunken Lycian ruins of Kekova Island and up to Simena Castle.

items: Enter Myra Ruins before 09:30 AM to beat midday sun inside the exposed Roman theatre.
Bring a light scarf or breathable cover-up if you prefer modest attire inside St. Nicholas Church (though it operates as a state museum rather than an active mosque).
Carry a passport photo on your phone for children under eight claiming free Ministry entry.
Reserve a waterfront table or private Kekova boat in Üçağız a day ahead during June–September.
Add the Museum of Lycian Civilizations at Andriake (five minutes from Demre) if you have an extra 90 minutes.

faq.q: How much time do you need at Myra and St. Nicholas Church?
faq.a: Allow 60 to 75 minutes for Myra's rock tombs and Roman theatre, plus 45 to 60 minutes for St. Nicholas Church. Including short drives and parking between them, three hours covers both sites without rushing.

faq.q: Is St. Nicholas Church an active church or a museum?
faq.a: It is a state-run memorial museum managed by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. Visitors do not need to observe mosque prayer closures, though modest, respectful dress is appreciated.

faq.q: Can you climb inside the Myra rock tombs?
faq.a: No. Barriers protect the lower cliff face to preserve the carved reliefs and inscriptions. However, the viewing paths sit close enough to see the funerary portraits and Lycian scripts clearly, especially with binoculars or a zoom lens.

faq.q: Is the MuseumPass The Mediterranean worth it just for Demre?
faq.a: Not for Demre alone, since Myra (€13) and St. Nicholas (€17) total €30. The €90 Mediterranean pass pays off only if you also visit major sites like Hierapolis/Pamukkale (€30), Patara (€15), Aspendos (€15), and Phaselis (€10) within seven days.

faq.q: Can you swim near Kekova after lunch in Üçağız?
faq.a: Yes. While swimming directly over the protected sunken ruins along Kekova Island is prohibited, boat captains stop at clear nearby bays such as Tersane Bay, Akvaryum Bay, and Gökkaya Bay.

faq.q: Are Demre's sites wheelchair or stroller accessible?
faq.a: St. Nicholas Church has stepped entry down to the ancient floor level, which limits wheelchair access to viewing areas. Myra has mostly flat gravel paths near the theatre and tombs, though uneven stones require assistance.
